description.narrative: "According to the National Institute of Meteorology (INAM), Tropical Cyclone Freddy made its second landfall in Mozambique on March11, between 6:00 pm and 8:00 pm local time, passing through the town of Macuze, Namacurra District, Zambézia Province , with maximum winds of 148 km/h and gusts of up to 213 km/h. The precipitation brought by Freddy reached more than 600mm in some places, namely in the districts of Marromeu (672mm), Mocuba (581mm), Milange (529mm) and Morrumbala (491mm). This precipitation is four times greater than the average monthly precipitation during the wet season. The heavy rains and flooding that are being experienced in ZambéziaProvince are a major concern as the cholera outbreak continues to spread. As of 19 March, the cumulativenumber of cholera cases was10,697 cases and 75 deaths in 36 active districts. According to the latest data from the National Institute for Disaster Risk Management (INGD), Cyclone Freddy affected a total of 253,466 people - in Zambezia (211,784 affectedand 53 reported dead), Sofala (33,435) Tete (6,834) Manica (1,182 ) and Niassa (231). In terms of damage, around 48,134 homes were partially or completely destroyed, while around 191,562 hectares were damaged and another 38,000 hectares were lost. About 52health facilities and 1,561 classrooms were also damaged. As of March 15, around 49,159 people have been displaced and 139 accommodation centers have been established.The numberof people affected is likely to increase further as the rains and floodingcontinue and further needs assessments are being conducted. The authorities report that an increase in the volume of water discharges is expected in the river basins of the Buzi, Pungoe, Licungo, Namacurro, Nioiode and Raragara and Zambezi (Shire River sub-basin and lower Zambezi), and Rovuma rivers, causing floods of moderate to high regimen. A worsening of urban and peri-urban floods is also expected in the city of Quelimane.The floods had alreadyaffected hectares of crops ready to be harvested, impactingfood security and the population's main source of income. Schools, health centers, homes, water and sanitation systems, roads were devastated. The main road running north-south through Mozambique is flooded north of the city of Quelimane in Zambézia province.The number of people in need generated by Freddy's second fall in Mozambique adds to the needs of more than 239,000 people in southern and central Mozambique affected by the floods and Freddy's first fall. Thefirst crash resulted in significant damage to infrastructure as more than 22,000 homes were affected, almost 14,000 were destroyed,60 health facilities were flooded and 1,265 km of roads were damaged. Of particular concern is the damage to agriculture, as 92,000hectares of crops have beenaffected, including in areas where 400,000 people are already food insecure. Cyclone FREDDY is one of the strongest cyclones ever recorded in the Southern Hemisphere and is considered the longest-lasting cyclone according to the World Meteorological Organization (WMO)."

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
